title: Dancers leaving for the Olympics and the Harlem All-Stars
summary: Bert Gibson and Buster Brown went with the Olympics tour; Green names the four Harlem All-Stars (Green, Baby Lawrence, Jimmy Slyde, Buster Brown) and Copasetics.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, that was Bert Gibson and the famous Gibson family; and Buster Brown of the Harlem All-Stars -- the four Harlem All-Stars which was Chuck Green, Baby Lawrence, Jimmy Sly, and Kind Sir, who was Buster Brown. That was for George Wein, see.
How did the other dancers react to these guys leaving to go to the Olympics?

Well, they really didn't know -- realize it. One of them, Buster Brown, he was in the Harlem All-Star -- that he was going to be included, because he was not -- he was away. He was doing something else at the time of tap happening -- "Reminiscing with Chuck Green." See, I think he was with Mura Dean at that time. And he was -- they was trying to get him to become a member, I think, of the Copesetics, you see. That's a -- all of this was honor in the mayor of Harlem, which was Bill Bojangles Robinson, you see.
So, there were a number of different
groups that were forming at this particular time?

Oh, yeah. Well, this group that formed before was born into the jazz festival, the full -- the Harlem All-Stars. That was with Illinois Jacquet, Milt Buckner and people like that; the great little jazz, Roy Eldridge. He's being held over now here in the -- in Foreign City at Jimmy Woods (sic) Ryan's, you know. And Jimmy Woods -- by the way, one of Roof Ellington's late brothers finds, he's a bassist. He lives over there in Paris. He was in the virtuso musicians we were with.
